newsitem.title: USA: Former Chicago congressman sentenced for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Former Chicago congressman sentenced for fraud.

text.p: Former Illinois Congressman Mel Reynolds, imprisoned since 1995 for having sex with an underage campaign worker, was sentenced in federal court on Tuesday to 6 1/2 years on a federal fraud conviction.

U.S. District Court Judge Charles Norgle said the sentence would be served concurrently with his current five-year prison term, meaning that if Reynolds is paroled in January from the state sentence he would still have to serve out the balance of his federal sentence.

Norgle also ordered Reynolds to pay $20,000 in restitution for defrauding banks and other lenders out of about $400,000 and spending $15,000 in campaign contributions on personal expenses. In April, a jury convicted him on 15 of 16 counts of fraud and violating campaign finance laws.

Reynolds resigned his congressional seat representing a predominantly Democratic South Side district after his 1995 conviction on statutory rape and obstruction of justice charges. He was first elected in 1992 and re-elected two years later.

Reynolds, a former Rhodes scholar who often spoke of his rise from the cotton fields of the South to Harvard University and the halls of Congress, tearfully admitted wrongdoing at his sentencing hearing.

The judge also received written appeals for leniency from Reynolds' estranged wife Marisol, with whom he has three children, and Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, who was believed to have paid for his defence.
